title: Senior Product Manager, Developer SDK & Platform
description:
BuildKit is a Series D developer infrastructure company ($80M ARR) building the toolchain that lets software teams ship faster. Our SDK is used by 40,000+ developers across 2,000 companies. We're hiring a Senior PM to own our developer SDK and the platform layer that powers it.

About the role:
- Own the SDK roadmap across our core languages (JavaScript, Python, Go) and the platform APIs that underpin them
- Drive PLG growth: own activation and expansion metrics for self-serve developer signups through to paid conversion — you'll instrument funnels, define activation criteria, and run experiments to improve free-to-paid rates
- Design and launch SDK pricing tiers and packaging — we're moving from flat-rate to usage-based and need someone who has owned this type of transition before
- Partner with DevRel and Developer Advocacy to build onboarding sequences that convert free developers to enterprise accounts
- Define and own the developer experience: SDK design, API reference, quickstarts, and integration catalog

What we're looking for:
- 7+ years of product management, with at least 3 in developer tools, APIs, or platform products
- You have owned a PLG growth loop end-to-end: funnel instrumentation, activation criteria, free-to-paid conversion optimization — not just analytics consumption, but running experiments and owning the metric
- You have made a real pricing decision: you have owned a packaging or tier structure for a developer product and can articulate the tradeoffs you made
- Experience at a company with $75M+ ARR — you understand what enterprise developer onboarding looks like at scale (10,000+ developers, complex SSO/SCIM provisioning, usage reporting)
- Deeply technical: you can read SDK code, write integration examples, and debate API design with your engineering team
- Remote OK, US-based

Nice to have:
- Experience with usage-based billing or consumption pricing models
- Background in observability, CI/CD, or infrastructure tooling
- You have contributed to or maintained an open-source SDK or library

Comp: $180k-$215k + equity
